# opnsense_caddy_reverse_proxy (Resource)

Caddy reverse proxy domains (**Services ▸ Caddy Web Server ▸ Reverse Proxy ▸ Domains**, plugin `os-caddy`). Handlers (`opnsense_caddy_handle`) route the requests of a domain to upstreams.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "opnsense_caddy_reverse_proxy" "app" {
  from_domain = "app.example.com"
  description = "app"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `from_domain` (String) Enter a domain name. For a base domain, use "example.com" or "opn.example.com". For a wildcard domain, use "*.example.com". Using a wildcard domain with subdomains requires a "DNS Provider" and the "DNS-01 Challenge" or a custom certificate.

### Optional

- `access_log` (Boolean) Enable HTTP request logging for this domain and its subdomains. This option is mostly used for troubleshooting. It will log every single request. Defaults to `false`.
- `accesslist` (String) Select an Access List to restrict access to this domain. If unset, any local or remote client is allowed access. Defaults to ``.
- `acme_passthrough` (String) Enter a domain name or IP address. The HTTP-01 challenge will be redirected to that destination. This enables an ACME Client behind Caddy to serve "/.well-known/acme-challenge/" on port 80. Caddy will reverse proxy the HTTP-01 challenge for this domain, and will still issue a certificate using the TLS-ALPN-01 challenge or DNS-01 challenge for itself. This option can be used for High Availability when using Caddy with a master and backup OPNsense. Defaults to ``.
- `basicauth` (Set of String) Select Users to restrict access to this domain. Basic Auth matches after Access Lists. If unset, any user is allowed access. Defaults to `[]`.
- `client_auth_mode` (String) "request" - Ask clients for a certificate, but allow even if there isn't one; do not verify it. "require" - Require clients to present a certificate, but do not verify it. "verify_if_given" - Ask clients for a certificate; allow even if there isn't one, but verify it if there is. "require_and_verify" - Require clients to present a valid certificate that is verified. One of `request`, `require`, `verify_if_given`. Defaults to ``.
- `client_auth_trust_pool` (Set of String) Choose multiple CAs or self-signed certificates from "System - Trust - Authorities". Client Auth is activated as soon as at least one certificate has been chosen. Important: Certificate revocation lists are not evaluated. If you need granular control, provide individual self-signed certificates for each device, and unset them to block access. Though keep in mind that if no certificate is left in this field, Client Auth will be deactivated. Defaults to `[]`.
- `custom_certificate` (String) Choose "Auto HTTPS" to get automatic "Let's Encrypt" or "ZeroSSL" certificates; no additional plugin required. Alternatively, choose a custom certificate from "System - Trust - Certificates" for this domain, e.g., certificates managed by the optional os-acme-client plugin. Defaults to ``.
- `description` (String) Enter a description for this domain. Defaults to ``.
- `disable_tls` (String) When choosing HTTP, automatic certificate management will be disabled and all traffic to and from this domain will be unencrypted. One of `0`, `1`. Defaults to `0`.
- `dns_challenge` (Boolean) Enable the DNS-01 Challenge for this domain. Requires a "DNS Provider" in "General Settings". This is only needed for wildcard domains, or when the default challenges can not be used due to restrictive firewall policies. Defaults to `false`.
- `dns_challenge_override_domain` (String) If using CNAME delegation for DNS-01 challenges, enter the target domain here. The DNS provider will manage TXT records at '_acme-challenge.targetdomain' instead of the certificate domain. Your configured DNS Provider must have write access to this target domain. For wildcard certificates, ensure the CNAME delegation covers the _acme-challenge label. This enables least-privilege setups or can be used as a workaround when the primary DNS provider lacks an API. Leave empty if your DNS Provider has a dedicated field for this. Defaults to ``.
- `dyn_dns` (Boolean) Enable or disable Dynamic DNS. Requires a "DNS Provider" in "General Settings". The DNS records of this domain will be automatically updated. A wildcard domain will create a "*.example.com" record. A base domain will create a "example.com" or "opn.example.com" record. Some providers need subdomains to set records for domains like "opn.example.com"; in that case use the checkbox in the subdomains tab. Defaults to `false`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Enable this domain. Defaults to `true`.
- `from_port` (Number) Leave empty to use ports 80 and 443 with automatic redirection from HTTP to HTTPS or choose a custom port. Don't forget to allow these ports with a Firewall rule. If the default ports have been changed in "General Settings", leaving this empty will use the chosen alternative ports instead. Defaults to `-1` (OPNsense default).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) UUID of the Caddy domain.
